prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single, objectively “best” dentist for implants in Miami — the right provider depends on your needs (medical complexity, esthetic goals, budget, insurance) and on the clinician’s training, experience and track record. I can help you find top options, but first here are practical points to guide your choice and the questions to ask.

Who should place your implant
- For surgical placement: look for an oral & maxillofacial surgeon or a periodontist. They have the surgical training to place implants and manage bone grafts or sinus lifts.
- For the final crown/restoration: a prosthodontist or an experienced restorative dentist often does the prosthetic phase (abutment and crown) for the best esthetic/functional result.
- Many excellent practices coordinate both phases in-house or work closely with specialists.

Important credentials & experience to check
- Specialty training (DDS/DMD + residency in OMFS, periodontics, or prosthodontics).
- Board certification or active membership in relevant organizations (AAOMS, AAP, AAID, ITI, etc.).
- Years of implant experience and number of implants placed.
- Use of modern diagnostics (CBCT/3D imaging), guided surgery, digital planning and CAD/CAM restorations.
- Before-and-after cases and patient testimonials.

Questions to ask at consultation
- Who will place the implant and who will restore it?
- How many implants like mine have you placed?
- Do you take CBCT scans and do digital planning/guide surgery?
- What are the risks, alternatives, and expected timeline?
- Will I need bone grafting or a sinus lift?
- What implant brand/system do you use and why?
- Can you show before/after cases and patient references?
- What is the all-in cost (implant, abutment, crown, grafts, followups)? Any warranties or guarantees?
- What are the sedation/anesthesia options?

Red flags
- Practitioners who do very few implants or won’t show case examples.
- Vague answers about costs or the implant system used.
- No pre-operative 3D imaging for complex cases.

Typical cost ranges (US general guide)
- Single implant (screw, abutment, crown): roughly $2,500–$6,000+ depending on complexity.
- Bone grafts/sinus lifts: additional $500–$3,000 or more.
(Prices vary widely by provider and case; get a written estimate.)

How I can help now
- If you’d like, tell me your Miami ZIP code or neighborhood and whether you prefer an oral surgeon, periodontist, or prosthodontist — I can find highly rated local providers, compare reviews, note specialties, and list contact info and typical patient ratings.
